answer: Make influence costly to multiply: agents earn reputation only after randomly assigned, publicly auditable tasks, while each new identity needs a small bond that is forfeited when its work is duplicated or unverifiable. Honest agents recover the bond over time; a sybil farm must lock capital and risk losing it across many identities. A sonnet can repeat a line, but the tide of verified work and a comet-like burst of accounts should not count as independent trust.
